definitions.explanation: A category of Japanese particles that attach to words to add nuances such as limitation, emphasis, inclusion, or approximation. Unlike case particles ({格助詞|かくじょし}) which mark grammatical roles, adverbial particles modify the meaning or scope of the word they attach to.

examples.japanese: 「は」は{副助詞|ふくじょし}に{分類|ぶんるい}される。
examples.english: "Wa" is classified as an adverbial particle.

examples.japanese: {副助詞|ふくじょし}の「も」は「{同様|どうよう}に」という{意味|いみ}を{加|くわ}える。
examples.english: The adverbial particle "mo" adds the meaning of "also" or "likewise."

examples.japanese: {日本語|にほんご}{文法|ぶんぽう}では、{副助詞|ふくじょし}と{格助詞|かくじょし}の{区別|くべつ}が{重要|じゅうよう}である。
examples.english: In Japanese grammar, the distinction between adverbial particles and case particles is important.

notes:
A grammatical term from {副|ふく} (secondary, adverbial) + {助詞|じょし} (particle). This is one of the standard particle categories in Japanese school grammar ({学校文法|がっこうぶんぽう}).

COMMON {副助詞|ふくじょし}:
- は: topic marker (also contrast)
- も: also, even
- こそ: emphasis (it is precisely...)
- さえ: even
- でも: even, or something
- しか: only (with negative)
- まで: even, as far as
- ばかり: only, nothing but
- など: and so on, such as
- くらい/ぐらい: about, approximately

OTHER PARTICLE CATEGORIES:
- {格助詞|かくじょし}: case particles (が, を, に, で, etc.)
- {接続助詞|せつぞくじょし}: conjunctive particles (て, ば, から, etc.)
- {終助詞|しゅうじょし}: sentence-final particles (ね, よ, か, etc.)
